solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Person in choir seeing offender losing name for good

indicators.note: N, the abbreviation for name, is dropped and G, the abbreviation for good, put in its place

parts.note: an offender is a sinner, one who transgresses

explanation.surface: A chorister is spotted with a wrongdoer who has lost his good name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who sings in a choir is a vocalist, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Keep watch on small gate receipts away from home

parts.note: the take is the money taken at an event, its gate
out means not at home

explanation.surface: A small club's ticket money is earned at away matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeout is surveillance of a place, so to stake out is to keep it under watch.

clue.text: Rising river in US city wanting attention

indicators.note: in says the reversed river goes inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A river floods a US city that needs care.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales and England, and in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A needy person lacks things, or craves attention and support.

clue.text: Modern entrepreneur is always protecting rear

indicators.note: protecting means one word guards the other by surrounding it

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
the tail is the rear end

explanation.surface: A forward-looking businessperson always watches their back.
explanation.definitionFit: An online retailer is a seller of the internet age, a newly coined kind of trader.

clue.text: Beast's protection — mostly by assent in Germany

parts.note: ja is German for yes

indicators.note: mostly says the word for protection loses its final letter

parts.note: a guard is a protection

explanation.surface: An animal's defences are mainly approved of in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beast's' is read as 'beast is', the 's joining definition to wordplay; 'mostly' trims GUARD to GUAR, and 'by' just places JA beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is a big cat of the Americas, an example of a beast.

clue.text: A strange notion of Salieri, for example

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of the following word are reordered

explanation.surface: An odd idea of the composer Salieri.
explanation.walkthrough: Antonio Salieri was an Italian composer, Mozart's rival in legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Salieri's first name was Antonio, so he is an example of someone so named.

clue.text: Brunel did badly without restraints

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are messed up, rearranged

explanation.surface: The engineer Brunel performed poorly when unchecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was a famous Victorian British engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridle restrains a horse, so lacking one means unrestrained.

clue.text: Novice is almost fleeced, with one taken in

indicators.note: taken in says the numeral one goes inside the shortened word
almost cuts the last letter from the synonym for fleeced

parts.note: rooked means swindled or fleeced
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A beginner is nearly swindled, having one person deceived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' sounds like 'deceived', fitting the fleecing surface, but is a container signal: I goes inside ROOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or recruit, a beginner in some activity.

clue.text: Expert on female wit gets one in hand

indicators.note: in an across clue 'expert on female' puts the expert's letters after the female's

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a card is a witty, amusing person

explanation.surface: A specialist in women who is also a joker wins one over.
explanation.definitionFit: A king, queen or jack is a court card, one of those you may hold in a hand at cards.

clue.text: Fails to protect single clergyman from Guides

indicators.note: to protect says the verb wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: an engine that dies fails
I, the Roman one, means single
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: Someone fails to shield an unmarried vicar from the Girl Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: Directories are reference books listing names and addresses, so guides to finding people.

clue.text: What's more, small child stifles exclamation of disapproval

indicators.note: stifles means the child's word smothers the exclamation, holding it inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child
boo is a jeer of disapproval

explanation.surface: A toddler suppresses a jeer, and furthermore something else happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms meaning in addition, besides.

clue.text: Tax frivolity, dismissing it

indicators.note: dismissing says the word it is sent away from the synonym

parts.note: levity is light-hearted frivolity

explanation.surface: A duty on light-heartedness is waived.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a charge or duty imposed by authority, a synonym for a tax.

clue.text: Stay in with girl worried about cause of hoarseness

indicators.note: worried suggests agitation, so the letters of the fodder are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stays home with an anxious daughter fretting about why she has lost her voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis, inflammation of the voice box, is a common illness that makes the voice hoarse.

clue.text: Studies fish by season

indicators.note: by places the fish next to the season, the season coming first

parts.note: summer is one of the four seasons
a school is a shoal of fish

explanation.surface: A naturalist examines fish according to the time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studies' looks like a verb but is a noun, a course of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer school is a course of study held during the holidays, so the plural noun fits loosely as studies.

clue.text: Dances for doctor working with escorts

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
on means functioning, working
to walk someone home is to escort them

explanation.surface: A doctor at work also escorts people to dances.
explanation.definitionFit: The moonwalk is a dance step, gliding backwards, made famous by Michael Jackson.

clue.text: Working croft in diocese at no cost at all

indicators.note: in says the reordered croft goes inside the diocese word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: working means the letters of croft are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone farms a smallholding in a church district without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: A croft is a small Scottish farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off scot-free is escaping without penalty or payment.

clue.text: Rum do, as her topic is a medical speciality

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, signalling that the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd affair, since her subject is a branch of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of medicine dealing with bones and muscles is a recognised specialism.

clue.text: First line in the representation of Scotland

indicators.note: in places the pieces for first and line inside the word the

parts.note: first is written 1st, and the 1 read as the letter I gives IST

explanation.surface: The opening words of a portrayal of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First line' reads as an opening verse, but splits into 1ST (as IST) and L; 'the' is also fodder, so 'the representation' only seems a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is Scotland's national emblem, a symbol representing the country.

clue.text: A fellow with good name in Germany for people in Asia

parts.note: F is short for fellow, as in FRS
Hans is a common German first name

explanation.surface: A man with a good German name is cast as people of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghans are the people of Afghanistan, a country in Asia.

clue.text: To cream off pay with no answer is revealing

parts.note: to skim is to cream off the top

indicators.note: with no says the letter for answer is taken out of pay

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Siphoning off wages without reply is telling.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothing is scanty and shows a lot of skin, so revealing.

clue.text: Script given to broadcaster generating letters on air

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster
script means handwriting, writing

explanation.surface: A screenplay is handed to a TV channel that produces messages on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a UK satellite TV company. 'On air' suggests broadcasting, but here means literally in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Skywriting is aircraft tracing letters in smoke across the sky, literally creating lettering in the air.

clue.text: Dislikes losing energy in top gear

indicators.note: losing says the abbreviation for energy is dropped from the verb

parts.note: to dislike strongly is to hate, so dislikes gives hates
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone hates losing drive in the fastest gear of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' evokes the car's highest gear (and the TV show), but means gear worn on top: headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Headwear is clothing, or gear, worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Foolhardy head turns up to trap monster

indicators.note: turns up says the hidden letters are read backwards
to trap says the answer is caught within the words around it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reckless leader arrives to catch a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'trap monster' as the definition, leaving the hidden word unsignalled; 'to trap' is the hiding indicator and 'monster' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was the many-headed serpent of Greek myth slain by Hercules.

clue.text: Charm a beast of burden till dropping sick

parts.note: a mule is a pack animal

indicators.note: dropping says the word for sick is removed from the word till

parts.note: taken as written
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A packhorse is enchanting until it falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till dropping sick' removes ILL from TILL, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a talisman worn to ward off harm, a lucky charm.

clue.text: Put up with a disheartened reverend being an accepted model

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it

indicators.note: disheartened means the middle letters are removed, leaving only the outside letters of reverend

explanation.surface: Tolerating a dispirited vicar who is a role model.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a benchmark, a norm that others are measured against.

clue.text: Agreeable people finding sun in peninsular state?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for sun inside the country's name

parts.note: Yemen lies on the Arabian Peninsula
S is short for sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: Finding sunshine in a nation on a peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who agree with everything their superiors say.

clue.text: Manage to get away, using key copy

parts.note: Esc is the ... key on a keyboard
to ape is to imitate or copy

explanation.surface: Someone flees with a duplicated key.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to break free or flee, so managing to get away.
